Kushan Empire: Greek. The Kushan Empire (c. 30–c. 375 CE) was a syncretic empire formed by the Yuezhi in the Bactrian territories in the early 1st century.

Almoravid dynasty: Berber. It established an empire that stretched over the western Maghreb and al-Andalus, starting in the 1050s and lasting until its fall to the Almohads in 1147.
Which country used the dinar as its official currency?
The dinar is the official currency of Volga Bulgaria. Volga Bulgaria was a multi-ethnic state with large numbers of Bulgars, Finno-Ugrians, Varangians, and East Slavs.

Once the Chief Mufti of a breakaway Chechen republic during the First Chechen War, this politician later switched allegiance to Moscow and became president of the Chechen Republic before being assassinated by a bomb at a 2004 Victory Day parade — who is he?

Akhmad Kadyrov (23 August 1951 - 9 May 2004) was a Russian politician and revolutionary who served as Chief Mufti of the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria in the 1990s during and after the First Chechen War.
Recognized as monarch while still a boy living in Switzerland, this king of Siam returned home in 1945 only to die under mysterious circumstances the following year — who was he?
Ananda Mahidol (20 September 1925 - 9 June 1946) was the eighth king of Siam (later Thailand) from the Chakri dynasty, titled Rama VIII.
Before he became the first governor of New South Wales, this British naval officer started out as an apprentice on a whaling ship and even spent time seconded to the Portuguese Navy — who was he?
Arthur Phillip (11 October 1738 - 31 August 1814) was a British Royal Navy officer who served as the first governor of the Colony of New South Wales.

Fought on September 19, 1356, during the Hundred Years' War, this clash saw Edward the Black Prince and 6,000 Anglo-Gascons defend a fortified position against 14,000 to 16,000 French attackers. Name it.
Battle of Poitiers was fought on 19 September 1356, during the Hundred Years' War, between a French army commanded by King John II and an Anglo-Gascon force under Edward, the Black Prince.
This French politician left a center-right party in 2017 to join Emmanuel Macron's new movement, then served as France's economy and finance minister from 2017 to 2024 — who is he?
Prince Frederick, Duke of York and Albany
Bruno Le Maire (born 15 April 1969) is a French politician, writer and former diplomat.
Born Ong Boon Hua in Sitiawan, this Maoist became a revolutionary at 15 and led the Communist Party of Malaya and its armed wing from 1947 until the party dissolved in 1989 — who was he?
Chin Peng (21 October 1924 - 16 September 2013), born Ong Boon Hua, was a Malayan communist politician, guerrilla leader, and revolutionary.

While working for the RAND Corporation, this military analyst leaked a top-secret Pentagon study on Vietnam War decision-making to major newspapers in 1971, later facing Espionage Act charges carrying up to 115 years — who is he?
Daniel Ellsberg (April 7, 1931 - June 16, 2023) was an American political activist, economist, and United States military analyst.
A former governor of California, he led the Supreme Court through Brown v. Board, Miranda, and Loving — and chaired the commission that probed JFK's assassination. Which chief justice?

Earl Warren (March 19, 1891 - July 9, 1974) was an American attorney and politician who served as the 30th governor of California from 1943 to 1953, and as the 14th chief justice of the United States from 1953 to 1969.
Manufactured by Airbus Helicopters under the designation EC665, this four-blade attack helicopter first entered service in 2003 — which aircraft?
Eurocopter Tiger is a four-blade, twin-engine attack helicopter which first entered service in 2003.

Radicalized at night school in Tokyo, this activist joined a communist faction advocating armed revolution in 1969, then went on to found and lead the militant group known as the Japanese Red Army. Who is she?
Fusako Shigenobu (born September 28, 1945) is a Japanese communist activist, writer, and the founder and leader of the now-disbanded militant group Japanese Red Army (JRA).
The youngest brother of Nicholas II, this Russian royal was briefly declared emperor after his sibling's 1917 abdication but declined to take power the very next day — who was he?
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia was Son of Tsar Alexander III (1878–1918).
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia
In Norse mythology, this female being presides over an underworld realm that shares her name, receiving a portion of the dead — who is she?
Hel (mythological being) (Old Norse) is a female being in Norse mythology who is said to preside over an underworld realm of the same name, where she receives a portion of the dead.
After earning a law doctorate from Cornell, which Taiwanese politician led the Legislative Yuan caucus for the Taiwan People's Party from 2024?
Huang Kuo-chang (pinyin: Hung Guchng; Peh-e-j: Ng Kok-chhiong; born (1973-08-19)19 August 1973) is a Taiwanese legal scholar and politician.

A Confederate cavalry general famous for being Robert E. Lee's eyes and ears, he cultivated a cavalier image: red-lined gray cape, ostrich-plumed hat cocked to one side, and a splash of cologne. Who was this dashing horseman?
J. E. B. Stuart (February 6, 1833 - May 12, 1864) was a Confederate cavalry general during the American Civil War.
This biblical queen, wife of King Ahab of Israel, was thrown from a window on the orders of Jehu and devoured by dogs, as the prophet Elijah had foretold — who was she?
Jezebel was the daughter of Ithobaal I of Tyre and the wife of Ahab, King of Israel, according to the Book of Kings of the Hebrew Bible (1 Kings 16).
This member of the First Triumvirate led the Gallic Wars, defeated Pompey, and sparked the political chaos that would end the Republic. Who?

Julius Caesar (12 or 13 July 100 BC - 15 March 44 BC) was a Roman general, statesman, and author who was the dictator of the Roman Republic almost continuously from 49 BC until his assassination in 44 BC.
Though named for one region, this Hohenzollern realm was actually based in the Margraviate of Brandenburg and rose from the work of 'The Great Elector.' What was it?
Kingdom of Prussia was a German state that existed from 1701 to 1918.
Born in Karnal to a wealthy Rajput family, this lawyer became the first prime minister of his newly founded nation and, revered as 'Leader of the Nation,' was assassinated in 1951 — who was he?
Liaquat Ali Khan (1 October 1895 - 16 October 1951) was a Pakistani lawyer, politician and statesman who served as the first prime minister of Pakistan from 1947 until his assassination in 1951.

Serving as the third and last Commonwealth president for barely five weeks in 1946, this man then became the first leader of the newly independent Philippine republic before dying in office in 1948 — who was he?
Manuel Roxas (January 1, 1892 - April 15, 1948) was the fifth president of the Philippines, serving from 1946 until his death in 1948.
Described in Genesis as the king of Salem and a priest of 'God Most High,' this biblical figure blesses Abram with bread and wine and is later invoked in the Epistle to the Hebrews — who is he?
Melchizedek was the king of Salem and priest of El Elyon (often translated as "God Most High").
Serving as the sixth chief of a major right-wing Hindu nationalist organization since 2009, this Indian activist was born in 1950 — who is he?

Mohan Bhagwat (born 11 September 1950) is an Indian activist who is serving as the sixth and current Sarsanghchalak (Chief) of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a right-wing Hindutva paramilitary organisation, since 2009.
Founded in 2023 by Pieter Omtzigt, what is the name of this Christian-democratic political party in the Netherlands?
New Social Contract is a Christian-democratic political party in the Netherlands founded by Pieter Omtzigt in 2023.
This November 1942 Allied invasion of French North Africa, a three-pronged strike at Casablanca, Oran and beyond, gave U.S. forces their first foothold against the Axis — what was it called?
Operation Torch (8-16 November 1942) was an Allied invasion of French North Africa during World War II.
Succeeding his father's abdication in 2013, this monarch is the eldest child of King Albert II and married Mathilde d'Udekem d'Acoz, with whom he has four children — who is he?
Philippe of Belgium (born 15 April 1960) is King of the Belgians, and is the eldest child of King Albert II and Queen Paola.
The first person from Uttar Pradesh and the first member of the BJP to hold the office, this Indian lawyer and politician served as his country's president from 2017 to 2022. Who is he?
Ram Nath Kovind (born 1 October 1945) is an Indian politician and lawyer who served as the president of India from 2017 to 2022.
Born in British Hong Kong and once a Member of Parliament, this academic and broadcaster now co-directs a grand-strategy program at Yale and co-hosts the podcast 'The Rest Is Politics' — who is he?
Rory Stewart (born 3 January 1973) is a British academic, broadcaster, writer, and former diplomat and politician.
This Austrian politician first became a government minister overseeing refugee integration in 2011, then served two separate terms as chancellor — who is he?
Sebastian Kurz (born 27 August 1986) is an Austrian former politician who served twice as Chancellor of Austria, first from 2017 to 2019 and then again from 2020 to 2021.
Documented in some form across Buddhism, Christianity, Vodou, Hinduism, Islam, and more, this altered state is attributed to control of the body by ghosts, demons, or deities — what is it called?
Spirit possession is an altered state of consciousness and associated behaviors purportedly caused by the control of a human body and its functions by spirits, ghosts, demons, angels, or deities.
One of the executioners of SA leader Ernst Röhm during the 1934 purge, this SS officer went on to command the Totenkopf Division before dying in an air crash in 1943 — who was he?
Grand Duke Konstantin Pavlovich of Russia
Theodor Eicke (17 October 1892 - 26 February 1943) was a German military officer who served as both a senior SS functionary and a Waffen-SS divisional commander in Nazi Germany.

Sparked when riot police suppressed a student demonstration on International Students' Day, this eleven-day, entirely nonviolent transition of power in November 1989 ended 41 years of one-party Communist rule in Czechoslovakia — name this event?
Velvet Revolution was a non-violent transition of power in what was then Czechoslovakia, occurring from 17 November to 28 November 1989.
This British statesman began his political career as a Conservative MP for Newark but became the face of the Liberal Party, serving a record four non-consecutive terms as Prime Minister — who is he?
William Ewart Gladstone (29 December 1809 - 19 May 1898) was a British statesman who served four times as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
This Chinese statesman served as the first Premier of the People's Republic of China from 1949 until his death in 1976, doubling as foreign minister for the first nine years — who is he?

Zhou Enlai (pinyin: Zhu nli; Wade-; 5 March 1898 - 8 January 1976) was a Chinese statesman, diplomat, and revolutionary who served as the first Premier of the People's Republic of China from October 1949 until his death in January 1976.

Nicknamed the 'Sheikh of slaughtering,' this Jordanian militant formed a group in 1999 before pledging allegiance to al-Qaeda's leader in 2004 and masterminding bombings during the Iraq War — who was he?
An Iranic nomadic people connected to the Yancai and Aorsi of ancient sources, this group dominated the Pontic-Caspian steppe before the Goths broke their hold in the 3rd century CE — who were they?
Alans: Ancient Iranic people of the North Caucasus.
Formed in 1993 by merging a party from West Germany with one from East Germany, this party held 85 of the Bundestag's 630 seats after Germany's 2025 election — which party?
Alliance 90/The Greens: Green political party in Germany.
Fought in 1879 between the British Empire and an African kingdom, this conflict included the defeat at Isandlwana and the defence of Rorke's Drift — which conflict?
Anglo-Zulu War: British colonial war in 1879. Two famous battles of the war were the Zulu victory at Isandlwana and the British defence at Rorke's Drift.
After conquering Kalinga in a brutal war around 260 BCE, this third Mauryan emperor turned to Buddhism and helped carry it across ancient Asia — who was he?
Ashoka: Mauryan emperor from 269 to 232 BCE.

A Brazilian naturalist who specialized in poison dart frogs — and has four frog species named after her — she also helped win women's suffrage in Brazil and signed the United Nations Charter. Who was she?
Bertha Lutz: Brazilian scientist and politician (1894–1976)
Lasting from 1858 to 1947, this era of Crown rule over the Indian subcontinent blended directly governed provinces with princely states under British paramountcy. What was it?
British Raj: 1858–1947 Crown colonial rule in India.

Identified chiefly by a shared family of Indo-European languages, this collection of ancient peoples included the Gauls, the Britons and Picts of Britain and Ireland, and the Galatians of Anatolia — who were they?
Celts: Collection of indo-European peoples sharing Celtic languages and cultural practices.
The Gospels present Jesus as the Son of God and say his coming as the messiah had already been prophesied. In which part of the Bible was that prophecy said to appear?

Christianity is an Abrahamic monotheistic religion based on the Bible and the teachings of Jesus. The Gospels state that Jesus is the Son of God and rose from the dead after his crucifixion, and that his coming as the messiah was prophesied in the Old Testament and chronicled in the New Testament.
This philosophical idea holds that all humans belong to a single community and should live as 'world citizens' guided by universal moral standards — what is it called?
Cosmopolitanism: Idea that all human beings are members of a single community.
A former co-owner of Talenti Gelato and Belvedere Vodka, this Minnesota congressman became the first Democrat to win his district in sixty years — who is he?
Dean Phillips: American businessman and politician (born 1969)

He mortgaged inherited farmland to invest in a software company he later sold to Microsoft for $1.1 billion, then became governor of North Dakota before serving as Secretary of the Interior — who is he?
Doug Burgum: American politician and businessman (born 1956)
The second of Islam's two main festivals, the Feast of the Sacrifice, falls on the 10th day of which month?
Eid al-Adha, the Feast of the Sacrifice, is the second of the two main festivals in Islam alongside Eid al-Fitr. It falls on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah.
An early ally of Hitler, he co-founded and led the Nazi Party's brownshirt paramilitary, the SA — until the SS assassinated him in 1934 during the Night of the Long Knives. Who was he?
Ernst Röhm: German Nazi military officer (1887–1934)
Founded in 1926 by Éamon de Valera after a split from Sinn Féin, which party has been one of Ireland's two dominant political forces ever since?
Fianna Fáil: Irish political party. The party dominated Irish political life for most of the 20th century, and, since its foundation, either it or Fine Gael has led every government.
Emerging from a wave of 1848 revolutions that toppled the monarchy, this government lasted only four years before an emperor's proclamation ended it in 1852. What was it called?

French Second Republic: Government of France from 1848 to 1852. The republic existed from 1848, when the monarchy fell, until its dissolution only four years later in 1852 upon the proclamation of the Second French Empire.
Born in colonial Virginia, this commander led the Continental Army to victory before serving as his nation's first president from 1789 to 1797 — who is he?
George Washington: U.S. Founding Father, president from 1789 to 1797.
A Siberian peasant turned wandering mystic, this faith healer won the trust of Tsar Nicholas II's family and vast sway in the Russian Empire's final years — who was he?
Adam of Bremen called this King of Norway the "Thunderbolt of the North" — a man who spent 15 years in exile commanding the Byzantine Empire's Varangian Guard before his crown. Who was he?
Alfonso VI of León and Castile
Harald Hardrada: King of Norway from 1046 to 1066.
The jealous wife and sister of Zeus, this queen of the Olympian gods presided over weddings and protected women in childbirth — who is she?
Hera: Goddess from Greek mythology, wife and sister of Zeus.
Officially known as Ansar Allah, this Zaydi Shia movement emerged in Yemen in the 1990s and is now backed by Iran as part of the 'Axis of Resistance.' Which group is this?
Houthis: Shia Islamist organization in Yemen.

Founded in 1885 as the first modern nationalist movement anywhere in the British Empire's Asian or African territories, this century-old big-tent party was later led by Mahatma Gandhi toward independence — which party?
Indian National Congress: Political party in India.
A former AFL quarterback turned nine-term congressman, this politician served as HUD secretary under George H.W. Bush before running for vice president alongside Bob Dole in 1996. Who is he?
Jack Kemp: American politician and football player (1935–2009)
This antimilitarist French socialist leader was assassinated in 1914 right as World War I broke out — who was he?
Grand Duke Konstantin Pavlovich of Russia
Jean Jaurès: French Socialist leader (1859–1914). The two parties merged in 1905 into the French Section of the Workers' International (SFIO).
Called "the Beautiful" and "the Good," this pious Byzantine emperor (1118-1143) spent his reign trying to undo the damage of Manzikert during the Komnenian restoration — who was he?
Alfonso VI of León and Castile

John II Komnenos: Byzantine emperor from 1118 to 1143. John II Komnenos or Comnenus (Greek: Ἱωάννης ὁ Κομνηνός, romanized: Iōánnēs Komnēnós; 13 September 1087 – 8 April 1143) was Byzantine emperor from 1118 to 1143.
Traditionally dominated by Jerusalem, this mountainous region of the Levant was renamed Syria Palaestina by the Romans after the Bar Kokhba revolt — what was it called?
Judea: Region in the Levant. The name is derived from the Hebrew name Yehudah, and was used during the Babylonian, Persian, Hellenistic, and Roman periods.
Leading a 1980 military coup that deposed Turkey's prime minister and abolished its parliament, this general later served as the country's 7th president — who was he?
Kenan Evren: 7th President of Turkey from 1982 to 1989.
Worshipped as the eighth avatar of Vishnu and central to the Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita, this major Hindu deity's birthday is celebrated as Janmashtami. Who is he?
Krishna: Major deity in Hinduism. The anecdotes and narratives of Krishna's life are known as Krishna Lila.

After his first wife, heir to the British throne, died in childbirth, this prince — offered the Greek crown following that country's war of independence — instead became first king of a newly independent European nation in 1831. Who was he?
Leopold I of Belgium: King of the Belgians from 1831 to 1865.

The only surviving son of Charlemagne and Hildegard, this Frankish co-emperor conquered Barcelona from the Emirate of Córdoba in 801 and briefly lost his throne for several months in 833–834. Who was he?
Louis the Pious: Emperor of the Carolingian Empire from 813 to 840.
Crowned after his father Alp Arslan died from battle wounds in 1072, this Seljuk ruler saw the empire reach its peak, though real power lay with vizier Nizam al-Mulk — who is he?
Malik-Shah I: Sultan of the Seljuk Empire from 1072 to 1092.
The son of Jupiter and Juno, this Roman deity oversaw both war and farming, and gave his name to the month that begins the campaigning season — who is he?
Mars (mythology): Roman god of war, guardian of agriculture.
This king of Sparta went to war after his wife Helen fled to Troy with the prince Paris, fighting alongside his brother Agamemnon — who was he?
Menelaus: King of Sparta, husband of Helen of Troy. In Greek mythology, Menelaus (Ancient Greek: Μενέλαος, Menélaos) was a king of Sparta.
Kentucky's longest-serving senator in state history, holding his seat since 1985, also became the longest-serving Senate party leader the country has ever had — who is he?
Mitch McConnell: American politician and attorney (born 1942)
Ruling twice as Ottoman sultan — first from 1421 to 1444, then again from 1446 until his death in 1451 — who was this 15th-century monarch?
Murad II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (r. 1421–1444, 1446–1451)
A former history professor and Georgia congressman who became the 50th Speaker of the U.S. House in 1995 and later ran for president in 2012 — which Republican is it?

Codenamed 'Hero' by the CIA and 'Yoga' by MI6, this Soviet military intelligence colonel's tips about missile installations helped the US spot Soviet weapons in Cuba and navigate the missile crisis without war — who is he?
Oleg Penkovsky: British spy in the USSR (1919–1963)
After seizing power in a 1961 coup, this South Korean army officer ruled as president until his assassination in 1979, presiding over rapid economic growth — who was he?
Park Chung Hee: President of South Korea from 1963 to 1979.
Possibly descended from Aegean migrants who settled Canaan's southern coast around 1175 BC, this Iron Age people organized their territory into a confederation of city-states — who were they?
Philistines: Ancient people who inhabited Canaan's southern coast.
This Macedonian Greek general, one of Alexander the Great's most trusted companions, retrieved his leader's body after his death and founded a new ruling dynasty in Egypt — who is he?
Ptolemy I Soter: Pharaoh of Egypt from 305 to 282 BC.
This Cuban revolutionary succeeded his brother as president in 2008 and served as the country's defense minister for nearly five decades — who is he?
Raúl Castro: President of Cuba from 2008 to 2018.
Abrasive and reactionary, this right-wing populist and economic nationalist served as New Zealand's 31st prime minister from 1975 to 1984 — who was he?
Robert Muldoon: Prime Minister of New Zealand from 1975 to 1984. After a troubled childhood, Muldoon served as a corporal and sergeant in the army in the Second World War.

On a single 1929 day in a Chicago garage, seven men were lined against a wall and gunned down — some of the killers disguised as police — in a brutal flashpoint of Prohibition-era gang warfare. What is this killing known as?

Saint Valentine's Day Massacre: 1929 gang shooting in Chicago. The Saint Valentine's Day Massacre was the murder of seven members and associates of Chicago's North Side Gang on Saint Valentine's Day 1929.

This wave of mass production, standardization, and rapid scientific discovery, sometimes dubbed the Technological era, is generally dated between 1870 and the outbreak of World War I in 1914. What period was this?
Second Industrial Revolution: 1870–1914 electrical and chemical era.
A writer who governed Tokyo from 1999 to 2012, this prominent ultranationalist was widely criticized for xenophobic and racist remarks against Chinese and Koreans in Japan — who was he?
Across religions this immortal, immaterial essence goes by many names — atman in Hinduism, jiva in Jainism, ruh in Islam — but what's its common English term?
Soul: In religion and philosophy, immaterial essence of a living being.
A 19th-century Muslim reformer and educationist in British India, he's widely credited as the father of the two-nation theory that underpinned the Pakistan movement — which figure was he?
Syed Ahmad Khan: Indian reformer and social activist (1817–1898)

Published by Anton LaVey in 1969, this text serves as the foundational scripture of a philosophy whose adherents describe themselves as 'atheistic' believers who see supernatural figures as projections of personality — which book?
The Satanic Bible: 1969 religious text of LaVeyan Satanism.
This movement campaigns for women to have the same legal right as men to go bare-chested in public, and also supports mothers' right to breastfeed openly — which cause?
Topfreedom: Social movement to allow female toplessness.
The only woman ever to serve as chief minister of Rajasthan, this Indian politician also held two Cabinet posts under Atal Bihari Vajpayee — who is she?

Vasundhara Raje: 11th Chief Minister of Rajasthan. Vasundhara Raje Scindia (born 8 March 1953) is an Indian politician, who has held the position of the chief minister of Rajasthan from 2003 to 2008 and 2013 to 2018.
The youngest member of China's Gang of Four, this politician organized the Shanghai People's Commune before being deposed and sentenced to life imprisonment after Mao's death — who is he?
Wang Hongwen: Chinese politician and activist (1935–1992)
Kenya's current president since 2022, he previously became the country's first elected deputy president after representing Eldoret North in parliament — who is he?

William Ruto: President of Kenya since 2022. William Kipchirchir Samoei Arap Ruto (born 21 December 1966) is a Kenyan politician who is the fifth and current president of Kenya since 13 September 2022.
A Tokyo-born artist tied to New York's Fluxus scene, she turned her 1969 honeymoon into a public protest and later recorded in the Plastic Ono Band — who is she?
Yoko Ono: Japanese artist and activist (born 1933)
Who among these four was born earliest?
William Osler (born 1849) is the earliest of the four. Osler created the first residency program for specialty training of physicians.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four. Lovelace is often considered the first computer programmer.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four. It is named after French mathematician, philosopher and physicist Blaise Pascal.
Who among these is a physicist?
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Ingrid Daubechies is a mathematician. Baroness Ingrid Daubechies ( doh-bə-SHEE; French: [dobʃi]; born 17 August 1954) is a Belgian-American physicist and mathematician at Duke University.
What is the atomic number of Copernicium?
Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.
What is the atomic number of Thallium?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
In what year did Johann Wolfgang von Goethe die?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 – 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
In what year was Nitrogen discovered?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
Which company manufactures Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: Skunk Works. It was the first operational aircraft to be designed with stealth technology.
Which country is Panavia Tornado from?
Panavia Tornado: Italy. It first flew on 14 August 1974 and was introduced into service in 1979–1980.
Who is credited with discovering Pavo?
Pavo (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Pavo is a constellation in the southern sky whose name is Latin for 'peacock'.
Who is credited with discovering Nitroglycerin?
Nitroglycerin: Ascanio Sobrero. It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
Who is credited with discovering Lithium?
Lithium: Johan August Arfwedson. Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

The only living member of its entire taxonomic order, this nocturnal African mammal digs into termite and ant hills using sharp claws and powerful legs — related distantly to elephants and manatees, what is it?
Aardvark (Orycteropus afer) is a medium-sized, burrowing, nocturnal mammal native to Africa.
A pioneer of industrial toxicology, this American physician trained at Michigan, worked out of Hull House in Chicago, and led the fight to curb lead poisoning in the workplace — who was she?
Alice Hamilton (February 27, 1869 - September 22, 1970) was an American physician, research scientist, and author.
Nicknamed the 'nail mosquito,' this genus — first classified in 1818 — is the sole mosquito genus known to carry human malaria — which genus is it?
Anopheles is a genus of mosquito first described by the German entomologist J. W. Meigen in 1818.
About a third of the several hundred mold species in this genus have a sexual reproductive stage, and some cause infections while others hold commercial value — which genus?
Aspergillus is a genus consisting of several hundred mold species found in various climates worldwide.
Ranging from 1 to 5 meters tall and found across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, this shrub genus's best-known species is the European type also called barberry — what genus is it?
Berberis is a large genus of deciduous and evergreen shrubs from 1-5 m (3+12-16+12 ft) tall, found throughout temperate and subtropical regions of the world (apart from Australia).
This branch of biology studies how plants have grown, reproduced, and evolved over the last 3.5 billion years of life on Earth — what field is it?
Botany is the branch of natural science and biology that studies the growth, reproduction and evolution of plants over the last 3.5 billion years of life on earth.

The largest land bird in North America went fully extinct in the wild in 1987 when every survivor was captured for breeding — which critically endangered vulture has since returned to the Grand Canyon and beyond?
California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.

Appearing in early childhood with symptoms like poor coordination and stiff or weak muscles, this group of movement disorders does not worsen over time even though symptoms become more noticeable in a child's first years — which condition?
Cerebral palsy (CP) is a group of movement disorders that appear in early childhood.
This tangor — a mandarin-orange cross — typically splits into seven to fourteen easy-to-peel segments — which fruit?
Clementine (Citrus clementina) is a tangor, a citrus fruit hybrid between a willowleaf mandarin orange (C. deliciosa) and a sweet orange (C. sinensis).
Born in 1863, this Italian mathematician is remembered chiefly as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
Corrado Segre (20 August 1863 - 18 May 1924) was an Italian mathematician who is remembered today as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry.
Affecting some 280 million people worldwide, this state of low mood saps motivation and the pleasure once taken in activities — what is it?
Depression (mood) is a mental state of low mood and aversion to activity.
Sometimes triggered by lead poisoning or reactions to neuroleptic drugs, this neurological disorder produces involuntary, twisting muscle contractions — what is it?

Dystonia is a neurological hyperkinetic movement disorder in which sustained or repetitive muscle contractions occur involuntarily, resulting in twisting and repetitive movements or abnormal fixed postures.
This Ancient Greek polymath, who became chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, is considered the founder of geography as a discipline and coined much of its early terminology — who is he?
The excessive buildup of collagen-rich connective tissue after chronic inflammation or repeated injury, leaving a permanent scar that can choke off organ function — what's this process called?
Fibrosis is the development of fibrous connective tissue in response to an injury.
Sometimes mistakenly called the 'stomach flu' even though it's unrelated to influenza, this inflammation of the gut is usually viral, with rotavirus the top cause in children. What condition is it?
Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract including the stomach and intestine.
The first of America's Teen Series fighters, this twin-tail jet with swing wings debuted at sea on the USS Enterprise in 1974. What is it?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat is an American carrier-capable supersonic, twin-engine, tandem two-seat, twin-tail, all-weather-capable variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the giant crab spider or cane spider, this member of the huntsman spider family is native to the tropics but has spread into subtropical areas — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria is a species of spider in the family Sparassidae, the huntsman spiders.
About the size of an almond in humans, this small brain region links the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland — what is it?
Hypothalamus (pl.: hypothalami; from Ancient Greek (hup) 'under' and (thlamos) 'chamber') is a small part of the vertebrate brain that contains a number of nuclei with a variety of functions.
The biggest cat in the Americas, it kills with a bite so powerful it can crack a turtle's shell — or punch straight through a mammal's skull between the ears. Which spotted predator is it?
Jaguar (Panthera onca) is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera that is native to the Americas.
This Indian aerospace engineer served as secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of both ISRO and the Space Commission — who is he?
K. Sivan (born 14 April 1957) is an Indian aerospace engineer who served as the secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of ISRO and Space Commission.

Seen using a silver stain and grown on media containing the amino acid cysteine, this genus of bacteria causes a severe pneumonia-like illness as well as a milder flu-like illness called Pontiac fever — name the genus?
Legionella is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria that can be seen using a silver stain or grown in a special media that contains cysteine, an amino acid.

Fatigue, memory problems, breathlessness, and sleep trouble that the WHO marks as setting in three months after infection — symptoms that vanish and reappear for weeks or years. What condition is this?
Long COVID is a group of health problems persisting or developing after an initial period of COVID19 from 2 infection.
An autosomal dominant flaw in the fibrillin-making FBN1 gene gives this disorder its tell-tale look — tall, long-limbed, double-jointed — while quietly threatening the aorta — what is it?
Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a multi-systemic genetic disorder that affects the connective tissue.
This British-Lebanese geometer co-founded topological K-theory and lent his name to a famous index theorem — and won both the Fields Medal and the Abel Prize. Who was he?
Michael Atiyah (22 April 1929 - 11 January 2019) was a British-Lebanese mathematician specialising in geometry.

Though its 83 species can grow as tall as trees, this genus is technically herbaceous, its 'trunk' just tightly wrapped leaf stalks, and it gives us edible bananas, plantains, and fiber for cloth — what genus is it?
Musa (plant) is one of three genera in the family Musaceae.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandin production, though it carries a risk of liver side effects. Name the drug?
Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this condition wears down joint cartilage over years, often first striking the knuckles nearest your fingertips and the base of the thumb — what is it?
Osteoarthritis is a type of degenerative joint disease that results from breakdown of joint cartilage and underlying bone.

Also known as underage medicine, this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — typically up to age 18 in most of the Commonwealth, but only 12 in India. Name the medical specialty?

Pediatrics (American English), also spelled paediatrics (British English) and also known as underage medicine, is the branch of medicine that involves the medical care of infants, toddlers, children, adolescents, and young adults.
When this domesticated mammal reached Europe from the Near East, it interbred so freely with local wild boar that scholars still argue whether it's a distinct species — what animal is it?
Pig (Sus domesticus), also called swine (pl.: swine) or hog, is an omnivorous, domesticated, even-toed, hoofed mammal.

Caused by the loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15, this rare genetic disorder leads to weak muscles and poor feeding in infancy, then constant hunger and risk of obesity in childhood — what's it called?

Prader–Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by a loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15. A similar mechanism occurs in Angelman syndrome, except the defective chromosome 15 is from the mother, or two copies are from the father.
This white, odorless nitroamine explosive, widely used since World War II, is the explosive agent inside C-4 plastic explosive — what is it called?
RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
Made by steaming dehusked oat groats before flattening them under heavy rollers and lightly toasting them, this whole-grain food becomes porridge when cooked — which product?
Rolled oats are a type of lightly processed whole-grain food.
Caused by a lack of vitamin C, this deficiency disease shows up after about a month of poor diet with weakness, sore limbs, gum disease, and bleeding from the skin — what is it?
Scurvy is a deficiency disease (state of malnutrition) resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
Unlike its shelled cousin the snail, this soft-bodied land mollusk gets by with no shell at all, or at most a tiny internal remnant of one — what animal is it?
Slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.
This Taiwanese-American software engineer co-founded and served as CTO of a massively popular video-sharing platform before later building MixBit through his company AVOS Systems — who is he?
Steve Chen (Wade-; born August 25, 1978) is a Taiwanese-American software engineer and Internet entrepreneur who is a co-founder and ex-CTO of YouTube.
Defined as applying conceptual knowledge to reach practical goals in a repeatable way, this field covers both tangible machines and intangible things like software — what is it?
Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.
What's the name for hardened, foul-smelling deposits of trapped debris that form in the crevices of the tonsils, sometimes visible as white flecks at the back of the throat?
Tonsil stones are mineralizations of debris within the crevices of the tonsils.
Occasionally causing hearing loss or bone marrow suppression as side effects, this IV antibiotic treats MRSA infections and, in oral form, a common gut infection - which drug?
Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic medication used to treat certain bacterial infections.
Short-legged, muscular, and stubby-tailed, this Australian marsupial can reach about a metre long and tip the scales between 20 and 35 kilograms — what is it?
Wombat are short-legged, muscular quadrupedal marsupials of the family Vombatidae that are native to Australia.
Found naturally in coffee, bread and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is produced when your liver partly oxidizes ethanol — making it a chief culprit behind the hangover. What is it?

Born as a Spanish CASA design and now built by a major European aerospace conglomerate, this twin-engine turboprop transport plane first flew in November 1997 and entered Spanish Air Force service in 1999 — which aircraft?
Airbus C295: European tactical military transport aircraft.
Nicknamed the death cap, this deadly poisonous fungus resembles edible species like Caesar's mushroom and is native to Europe — what is it?
Amanita phalloides: Poisonous mushroom (death cap). The large fruiting bodies appear in summer and autumn; the caps are generally greenish in colour with a white stipe and gills.
Native to the eastern Mediterranean, this flowering herb's seeds taste similar to fennel, licorice, and tarragon and flavor candies and spirits — what is it?
Also called gobō, this Eurasian plant is cultivated in Japan for its edible root but has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils elsewhere — which species?
Arctium lappa: Species of flowering plant. It has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils in North America, Australia, and other regions, but is cultivated for its vegetable root.
Developed to herd livestock across rough terrain by nipping at their heels, this short-coated working breed's coat reads as either 'red' or 'blue' — which breed?

Australian Cattle Dog: Breed of herding dog. The Australian Cattle Dog, or simply Cattle Dog, is a breed of herding dog developed in Australia for droving cattle over long distances across rough terrain.
With more than 2,000 species and petals but no sepals, this flowering plant genus originated in Africa and is popular as an ornamental houseplant in cooler climates — which genus?
Begonia: Genus of perennial flowering plants.
This medium-sized antelope of India and Nepal sports corkscrew horns up to 30 inches long and a striking two-tone coat, with white around the eyes set against black face stripes — which animal?
Blackbuck: Antelope native to India and Nepal. The blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.

This infraorder of decapod crustaceans tucks a stubby tail-like abdomen under a hard shell and ends its front pair of legs in pincers — over 1.5 million tonnes of them are eaten by humans yearly. What group is it?
Brachyura: Crustacean. The true crabs are the largest of the crab decapod groups with carcinised body forms.
A cole crop related to broccoli, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts, the heaviest recorded head of this leafy vegetable weighed nearly 138 pounds — what is it?
Cabbage: Leafy vegetable in the flowering plant family Brassicaceae.
This infraorder of decapod crustaceans is the true taxonomic home of what everyone actually calls a shrimp, found in fresh and salt water worldwide — what is it?
The largest part of the brain, this structure houses the cerebral cortex plus the hippocampus and basal ganglia, and works with the cerebellum to control every voluntary action. What is it?
Cerebrum: Large part of the brain containing the cerebral cortex.
Selected from over 11,000 applicants for NASA's Teacher in Space Project, this Concord, New Hampshire educator died aboard the Challenger in 1986 — who was she?
Christa McAuliffe: American teacher and astronaut (1948–1986)
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy, this opiate is a prodrug of morphine often paired with paracetamol to treat mild pain, coughs, and even diarrhea — what is it?
Codeine: Opiate and prodrug of morphine used to treat pain. It usually starts working after half an hour, with maximum effect at two hours.
Also known as the Cornelian cherry, this dogwood-family shrub or small tree is native to western and southern Europe as well as southwestern Asia — what's its scientific name?
Cornus mas: Species of flowering plant in the family Cornaceae.
This closed sac in the body, distinct from an abscess of pus, forms a shell of abnormal cells and may contain air, fluid, or semi-solid material — what is it, medically?
Cyst: Closed sac growth on the body. A cyst is a closed sac in the body, having a distinct envelope and division compared with the nearby tissue.

Found in many cough and cold medicines, this morphinan-class compound was approved by the FDA in 2022 as part of a rapid-acting antidepressant combo, but can act as a dissociative hallucinogen at high doses. What substance is it?
Dextromethorphan: Cough suppressant and dissociative drug.
Sold over the counter as Unisom and combined with vitamin B6 to ease morning sickness, this first-generation antihistamine is one of the world's most widely used sleep aids — which drug?
Doxylamine: First-generation antihistamine used as a short-term sedative and hypnotic (sleep aid)
Appointed to the Supreme Court by Barack Obama in 2010, this former Harvard Law dean became the fourth woman ever to serve as a justice — who is she?
Elena Kagan: US Supreme Court justice since 2010.
A rod-shaped gut bacterium that's mostly harmless or even helpful — some strains produce vitamin K2 and fend off nastier microbes — what is its name?
Sold in Italian restaurants as branzino, this slow-growing ocean fish is the most important species farmed commercially in the Mediterranean — what fish is it?
European seabass: Species of fish. It is one of only six species in its family, Moronidae, collectively called the temperate basses.
This beetle family produces light mainly at twilight to attract mates — though some females mimic another species' flash pattern just to lure and eat the males — what are they commonly called?
Firefly: Family of beetles. The Lampyridae are a family of elateroid beetles with more than 2,400 described species, many of which are light-emitting.
Only chefs with three-plus years of rigorous training may legally prepare this potentially lethal Japanese pufferfish dish, whose poison is tetrodotoxin — what is it?
Recognized as the world's longest ray-finned fish, this ribbon-shaped, silvery-blue deep-sea creature is often blamed for sea-serpent legends — which fish?
Giant oarfish: Species of oceanic ray-finned fish.
Dating back roughly 250 million years to the early Triassic, this ground-dwelling insect hears through an organ on its abdomen and leaps away from danger using powerful hind legs — what is it?
Grasshopper: Common name for a group of insects.
The son of a famous physicist and his first wife, this Swiss-American engineer taught hydraulic engineering at Berkeley and became renowned for research on sediment transport — who is he?

Hans Albert Einstein: Swiss-American engineer and educator. Hans Albert Einstein (May 14, 1904 – July 26, 1973) was a Swiss-American engineer, the second child and first son of physicists Albert Einstein and Mileva Marić.
In this condition, part of the stomach slips upward through the diaphragm into the chest, often triggering acid reflux, heartburn, or trouble swallowing — what is it?
Hiatal hernia: Entrance of abdominal organs into the middle chest through the diaphragm.
Also called prussic acid, this toxic, flammable liquid with the formula HCN boils just above room temperature and serves as an industrial precursor to plastics and mining chemicals — what is it?
Native to the subcontinent, the male of this bird species is called a peacock and sports a fan-shaped crest with a dazzling train of eyespot feathers used in courtship — which species?
Indian peafowl: Species of bird. The Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), also known as the common peafowl, or blue peafowl, is a species of peafowl native to the Indian subcontinent.
This American climatologist's 1988 Congressional testimony helped awaken the public to global warming, and he later turned activist — getting arrested more than once for the cause. Who is it?
A former Navy SEAL turned physician, this NASA astronaut flew to the International Space Station in 2025 as part of Expedition 72/73 after earning a Silver Star for valor in combat — who is he?
Jonny Kim: American astronaut, physician, and former U.S. Navy SEAL (born 1984)
Made from shredded pastry dough layered with cheese and soaked in sugar syrup, this Arab dessert is especially popular during Ramadan, with a famous variant hailing from Nablus — what is it?

One of the five big cats in the genus Panthera, this slender, muscular predator wears dark spots clustered into rosettes and is split today into eight recognised subspecies across Africa and Asia — what is it?
Leopard: Species of cat native to Africa and Asia.

This American stealth strike fighter comes in three flavors — conventional, short-takeoff/vertical-landing, and carrier-based — and with 883 in service is the world's fourth-most-numerous military aircraft. What is it?

Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II: American stealth multirole fighter aircraft. The Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II is an American family of single-seat, single-engine, supersonic stealth strike fighters.
Element number 12 is so eager to ignite that, once lit, it burns with a brilliant-white light — this lightweight alkaline-earth metal, less dense than aluminium, is what?
Magnesium: Chemical element with atomic number 12 (Mg)

This field studies abstract things like numbers, shapes, sets and probabilities, using logical proof to establish truths it calls theorems — and its branches include algebra, geometry and number theory. What is it?
Mathematics: Field of knowledge. Mathematics is a field of knowledge concerned with abstract concepts such as numbers, geometric shapes, sets, functions, and probabilities.
Discovered in 1893 and existing as two mirror-image enantiomers, this CNS stimulant is best known in its hydrochloride-salt form nicknamed 'crystal' — what is it?

A hemiparasitic plant that taps into its host tree via a structure called the haustorium to steal water and nutrients, its European species was introduced to Northern California in 1900 — what plant is it?
Mistletoe: Common name for various parasitic plants.

Grouping over 30 inherited disorders that cause progressive weakening and wasting of skeletal tissue — with the Duchenne form affecting roughly half of all cases in young boys — what's this disease group called?
Muscular dystrophy: Diseases in which skeletal and visceral muscles break down over time.

First arising in wormlike organisms 550 to 600 million years ago, this body-wide network splits into a central hub of brain and spinal cord and a peripheral web of nerve fibers relaying signals to and from every body part — which network?
Nervous system: Part of an animal that coordinates actions and senses.
This burrowing, semiaquatic South American rodent munches river-plant stems and was shipped worldwide by fur farmers, only to become a destructive invasive pest — which animal is it?
Nutria: Semi-aquatic rodent from South America.
In young children it can mean ear-pulling, extra crying, and poor sleep; it's a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear, from acute infections to lingering fluid. What's the medical name?
Otitis media: Inflammation of the middle ear. One of the two main types is acute otitis media (AOM), an infection of rapid onset that usually presents with ear pain.
Found in mice, cats, birds, humans, and dogs but absent in whales and most reptiles, this triangular bone is the body's largest sesamoid — what is it?
Patella: Kneecap, bone covering knee joint.
Known on the street as 'angel dust,' this dissociative anesthetic acts as an NMDA receptor antagonist and can cause hallucinations and psychosis — what is this drug?
Phencyclidine: Dissociative hallucinogenic drug, mostly used recreationally.

Commonly known as plantains or fleaworts — though unrelated to the banana-like cooking fruit of the same name — this genus of roughly 200 mostly herbaceous flowering plants tops out around 24 inches tall. Which genus?
Plantago: Genus of flowering plants. Plantago is a genus of about 200 species of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae, commonly called plantains or fleaworts.
This glucocorticoid medication used to suppress the immune system is actually a prodrug that the liver must convert into its active form before it works — what is it?
Prednisone: Steroid medication. It is also used to treat high blood calcium due to cancer and adrenal insufficiency along with other corticosteroids.
Often starting as a blood clot in the leg that travels to the lungs, this blockage can cause chest pain on breathing in, coughing up blood, and sudden death — what is the condition?

Pulmonary embolism: Blockage of an artery in the lungs. Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a blockage of an artery in the lungs by a substance that has moved from elsewhere in the body through the bloodstream (embolism).

Native to the eastern Himalayas and southwestern China, this small mammal sports dense reddish-brown fur, a ringed tail, and curved semi-retractile claws for climbing — and was the original bearer of its famous name. What is it?
Red panda: Species of mammal in Asia.
First created in 1994 near Darmstadt, Germany, this extremely radioactive synthetic element is named for the physicist who discovered X-rays — which element is it?
Roentgenium: Chemical element with atomic number 111 (Rg)
Also called elder or elderberry, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries are traditionally used to make cordial and wine — what's its scientific name?
Sambucus nigra: Species of flowering plant in the moschatel family.
When an infection-triggered immune overreaction sends blood pressure plummeting and disrupts cells throughout the body, doctors in the ICU are treating this life-threatening condition — what is it?
Septic shock: Dangerously low blood pressure due to damage from an organ infection.

Its last natural case appeared in 1977, and in 1980 the WHO declared it the only human disease ever wiped off the Earth — which scourge, known for fluid-filled blisters that scarred survivors, was it?
Commonly nicknamed phlegm, this mucus coughed up from the trachea and bronchi is examined for tell-tale yellow or green coloring that signals infection — what is it?
Sputum: Mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways.

Serving under both Presidents Sukarno and Suharto, this Indonesian economist held posts across trade, finance, and research ministries, and once lobbied Washington against Dutch colonial rule — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo: Indonesian statesman and economist (1917–2001)
Predicted by Mendeleev decades before its discovery and sitting in the periodic table between manganese and rhenium, what is the lightest element whose isotopes are all radioactive?
Technetium: Chemical element with atomic number 43 (Tc)
Native to the Mediterranean and a member of the mint family Lamiaceae, this dried herb's most common culinary variety, Thymus vulgaris, hails from Southeast Europe — what is it?
Thyme: Culinary herb. Thyme is a culinary herb consisting of the dried aerial parts of some members of the genus Thymus of flowering plants in the mint family Lamiaceae.
Its name translates to 'three-horned face,' and this frilled dinosaur roamed present-day western North America right up until the asteroid strike 66 million years ago — what dinosaur is it?
Triceratops: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur.

Known by names like lingonberry and cowberry, this evergreen shrub's tart berries are a Nordic cuisine staple and are commercially grown in the Pacific Northwest and the Netherlands — what is its scientific name?
Vaccinium vitis-idaea: Species of shrub with edible fruit.
Tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless, this polar molecule's strong hydrogen bonding makes it the solvent inside every known living organism — yet it offers no food energy at all. What is it?
Water: Chemical compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
This Greek economist served as Finance Minister under Alexis Tsipras during the 2015 debt crisis, becoming internationally known for battling EU-imposed austerity — who is he?
Yanis Varoufakis: Greek economist and politician (born 1961)
Mendelevium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for mendelevium is Md. Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md and atomic number 101.
What is the chemical symbol for ytterbium?
The symbol for ytterbium is Yb. Ytterbium is a chemical element; it has symbol Yb and atomic number 70.

Which of these is a comedian?
Sebastian Maniscalco is a comedian. Sebastian Maniscalco (Italian: [maniˈskalko]; born July 8, 1973) is an American stand-up comedian and actor.
In what year was Rachel Weisz born?
Rachel Weisz: Rachel Hannah Weisz (born 7 March 1970) is a British actress.
In what year was Sarah Jessica Parker born?
Sarah Jessica Parker (born March 25, 1965) is an American actress and television producer.
In what year was Rachel McAdams born?
Rachel McAdams: Rachel Anne McAdams (born November 17, 1978) is a Canadian actress.
In what year was Natasha Richardson born?
Natasha Richardson: Natasha Jane Richardson (11 May 1963 – 18 March 2009) was an English actress.
In what year was Hrithik Roshan born?
Hrithik Roshan: Roshan has frequently collaborated with his father, Rakesh Roshan.
In what year was Paul Rudd born?
Paul Rudd: Paul Stephen Rudd (born April 6, 1969) is an American actor.
In what year was Idris Elba born?
Idris Elba: Sir Idrissa Akuna Elba ( IH-driss; born 6 September 1972) is an English actor, DJ, rapper, and producer.
In what year was Jodie Foster born?
